issues.issue: Did the Crown withdraw its argument that the trial judge erred on the legal effect of his factual findings?
issues.applicant_position: Crown first argued the judge erred on the legal effect of his findings, then withdrew that argument before the hearing.
issues.result_quote: the Crown withdrew its arguments supporting the second question regarding the legal effect of the trial judge’s factual findings

issues.issue: Did the trial judge fail to consider all the evidence, including the Craigslist ads?
issues.applicant_position: Judge piecemealed the evidence under the criminal standard and ignored the Craigslist ads and other witnesses.
issues.respondent_position: Judge properly considered the other witnesses' evidence and all documentary evidence, so there is no error.
issues.result_quote: I see no error that warrants our intervention on this issue.

issues.issue: Did the trial judge assess the violence evidence on a wrong legal principle, misapprehending the evidence?
issues.applicant_position: Judge wrongly treated the other witnesses' evidence of violence as past discreditable conduct, though it is relevant to actus reus and exploitation.
issues.respondent_position: Mischaracterization did not taint the analysis: the judge admitted the violence evidence and considered it.
issues.result_quote: I conclude that the trial judge committed an error of law when he held that the evidence of regular violence and threats of violence

issues.issue: Might the error of law have had a material bearing on the acquittals?
issues.applicant_position: The error could have changed the verdict, since the judge's reasonable doubt and credibility findings rested on that evidence.
issues.respondent_position: Error did not affect the actus reus analysis, since the judge admitted the violence evidence and it was relevant.
issues.result_quote: This error can reasonably be thought, in the concrete reality of the case at hand, to have had a material bearing on the acquittals
